entries.title: Revelation of John 21:1
segments:
The apostle has a glorious vision of the blissful abode of the righteous after the general resurrection and judgment, under the form of a new heaven and a new earth, into which he sees descending from heaven the new Jerusalem, the abode of God and the Lamb. Thus the new earth becomes the dwelling-place of God; and death, suffering, and sorrow are done away for ever. 
 
  A new heaven and a new earth;  compare

.  These words express the greatness and the glorious character of the change that takes place in both the abode and the state of the redeemed.  Happy are they that shall have a place in the new Jerusalem.  They shall understand, as we cannot now, the meaning of this chapter.  No more sea; the absence of sea is understood by some to denote symbolically the absence of all change, commotion, or trouble of any sort.  But perhaps the words have a meaning which nothing but the appearance of the new heavens and new earth can explain.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:2
segments: Adorned for her husband; in the glorious apparel of perfect righteousness.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:3
segments: The tabernacle of God is with men; expressive of his intimate and perpetual communion with them.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:5
segments: When all things earthly are dissolved, and the treasures of the wicked are lost for ever, the righteous will enter into heaven and take possession of durable riches and righteousness, treasures incorruptible, undefiled, and never to fade away.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:6
segments: He said; Christ is the speaker.  It is done; the great work of man's redemption is accomplished.  The righteous are gathered into the new Jerusalem, and the wicked cast into the lake of fire.  The apostle is carried forward in vision to the end of all things, and looks back upon the prophecies of this book as already accomplished.  I am Alpha and Omega; see note to <Re 1.8>.  I will give unto him that is athirst; that thirsts for the living waters of salvation.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:7
segments: He that overcometh; he that successfully resists the temptations of the world, the flesh, and the devil, and continues steadfast in the belief and practice of the truth to the end.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:8
segments: The fearful; those who are afraid to do right lest they should suffer for it, and who neglect their duty to avoid trials, or escape dangers.  The second death; a death consisting in everlasting punishment with the devil and his angels.

. 
 
True courage is a distinguished virtue, and cowardice a great sin.  Those who dare not do right lest they should suffer for it, are cowards, and are ripening, with idolaters, liars, and murderers, to suffer the second death.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:9
segments: The seven vials;
.  The bride; the church in glory.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:10
segments: A great and high mountain; whence he could have a clear vision of the city descending out of heaven to men.  Compare
.  The holy Jerusalem; a symbol of the church in glory.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:12
segments: Twelve gates; twelve is the symbol of God's people.  Compare the twelve tribes of the Old, and the twelve apostles of the New Testament.  Hence this number prevails in the description of the new Jerusalem. Twelve angels; to guard them against the entrance of the unholy,
.  Thereon; on the gates.  The names of the twelve tribes; showing that all God's true people have a share in the city.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:13
segments: On the east three gates--on the west three gates; the perfect symmetry of the city is a symbol of its perfection.  See note to

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:14
segments: Twelve foundations--twelve apostles; compare
.  As there is one gate to each tribe, so is there also one foundation to each apostle.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:16
segments: Four square; the square has no disproportion on any side.  Here it is the appropriate symbol of completeness and perfection.  Twelve thousand furlongs; fifteen hundred Roman miles. This is to be understood of the city itself, which the apostle sees in vision as one vast structure towering up to heaven.  The wall which surrounded the city was distinct from it,

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:17
segments: A hundred and forty and four cubits; that is, twelve times twelve cubits in height.  The measure of a man, that is, of the angel; it is the measure of a man, as being such a measure as men commonly use; and the measure of the angel, because an angel now employs it.  If we reckon a cubit at from eighteen to twenty inches, one hundred and forty-four cubits will equal from two hundred and sixteen to two hundred and forty feet.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:18
segments: Jasper--gold--all manner of precious stones; showing the beauty, excellence, and glory of the heavenly city.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:21
segments: Things most esteemed on earth are used to represent things in heaven, in order to give men the highest and best ideas of them.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:22
segments: No temple; the church in glory needs no particular place or time set apart as holy in distinction from the rest, or especially consecrated to the worship of God; for all space and all duration are holy, holy, holy, being filled with the presence of God and the Lamb.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:23
segments: No need of the sun; for the presence of God and the Lamb makes perfect, eternal day.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:24
segments: Their glory and honor; every thing desirable, excellent, and glorious, is perfected and perpetuated in heaven.

entries.title: Revelation of John 21:27
segments:
They which are written; chosen of God, renewed, justified, sanctified, and thus fitted to be glorified. 
 
Here the righteous and the wicked dwell together in the same country, the same city, and the same family, and are united by numerous relative, social, and civil ties; and dwell in places as diverse and distant as heaven is from hell.
